sources.entry: CapRover | Easy app and database deployment and web server manager

summary.one_liner: CapRover is a self-hosted platform for deploying apps and databases and managing a web server, with a web GUI and CLI, built on Docker, nginx, and Let's Encrypt.
summary.what_it_does: CapRover lets you deploy NodeJS, Python, PHP, ASP.NET, Ruby, and Go applications, plus databases such as MariaDB, MySQL, MongoDB, and Postgres, from a dropdown-style interface. It runs on Docker Swarm for containerization and clustering, and uses nginx (with a customizable template) for load balancing. Free SSL certificates come from Let's Encrypt, and NetData is used for monitoring. It offers both a web GUI and a CLI for automation and scripting. The README says removing CapRover leaves deployed apps running.
use_cases: deploy a NodeJS or Python app to my own server
self-host databases like MySQL or MongoDB with one click
set up a web server without learning nginx or Docker
automatic free HTTPS certificates for my apps
reduce hosting costs compared to Heroku-style platforms
script app deployments from the command line
how_to_run: Head over to the "Getting Started" section of the documentation (linked from the README; the README does not give the commands inline)
notable: No Docker or nginx knowledge required; deploy via web GUI or CLI
Removing CapRover leaves deployed apps running (no lock-in)
Customizable nginx template for load balancing
One-click installation of common databases such as MariaDB, MySQL, MongoDB, and Postgres
caveats: README does not list server requirements or supported platforms; setup details are only in the external documentation
Installation instructions are not included in the README itself
keywords: deploy my app to my own server
